backlog.title: [CapAuth] Make Nextcloud signing-key custody check optional
backlog.description:
Update the CapAuth source repository so `capauth doctor custody` does not report a hard failure for installations that do not use or publish the Nextcloud integration.

Context:
- Observed with CapAuth 0.3.1 at source commit `183c04a7c623e8abcf37bd705bf8bca1deb4a364`.
- `src/capauth/custody.py::run_custody_checks()` unconditionally calls `check_nextcloud_signing_key()`.
- The only current override, `CAPAUTH_NEXTCLOUD_KEY`, changes the expected path; it cannot declare the integration out of scope.
- This installation has never created a Nextcloud signing key. Casey/Jarvis PGP identity, revocation, keypair, keystore/expected warning, backup, and restore checks are otherwise healthy.
- Do not create a dummy key or point the check at a placeholder merely to make the doctor green.

Proposed behavior:
- Add an explicit policy/config option such as `CAPAUTH_REQUIRE_NEXTCLOUD_SIGNING_KEY=true|false` or an equivalent custody declaration field.
- Preserve secure default behavior for deployments that publish the Nextcloud app.
- When explicitly disabled, report `nextcloud_signing_key` as N/A/SKIP (or WARN if the current result schema cannot represent N/A), and do not make the overall doctor result fail.
- Ensure the report clearly distinguishes “integration not enabled” from “required key missing.”

Acceptance criteria:

done.title: [SKL-S2-01][L] Build the read-only HammerTime release and artifact adapter
done.description:
## Corrected completion evidence (codex-skl-s2-01-fix, 2026-08-21)

Corrected the read-only HammerTime adapter after independent review. Legacy authorization now occurs before registry or filesystem discovery, with a coarse fail-closed decision followed by an exact-path decision. Public legacy resolution returns a typed LegacyPathResolution pinned to both the record bytes and registry snapshot. ResolvedRelease pins the alias snapshot, LegacyMatterRecord pins the registry, and PacketReference pins optional review artifact bytes.

All rooted filesystem traversal now uses directory-relative descriptors with O_NOFOLLOW and O_DIRECTORY. Every opened descriptor is verified under the configured root and outside every Inbox path component. Fixed file symlinks, fixed directory symlinks, symlinks into synthetic Inbox, traversal, and descriptor target changes fail closed. The adapter still has no write, move, delete, or dispatch surface.

### Files changed by this correction
- packages/connectors/hammertime/README.md
- packages/connectors/hammertime/src/sklegal_hammertime/__init__.py
- packages/connectors/hammertime/src/sklegal_hammertime/adapter.py
- packages/connectors/hammertime/src/sklegal_hammertime/models.py
- tests/test_hammertime_adapter.py

scripts/run_checks.sh was not edited by this card. Its concurrent S1-07 automatic discovery change includes tests/test_hammertime_adapter.py.

### Tests and exact results
- .tools/bin/uv run --locked pytest -q tests/test_hammertime_adapter.py: 54 passed, 7 subtests passed in 0.32s.
- .tools/bin/uv run --locked python -m unittest -v tests.test_hammertime_adapter: Ran 54 tests in 0.136s, OK.
- ./scripts/run_checks.sh unit-test: PASS, discovered 25 Python unit modules including tests/test_hammertime_adapter.py; adapter module 54 passed and 7 subtests passed; web suite 9 files and 85 tests passed.
- .tools/bin/uv run --locked pytest -q tests/integration/test_foundation_contract.py tests/integration/test_domain_contract.py tests/integration/test_capauth_contract.py: 10 passed, 51 subtests passed in 0.64s.
- .tools/bin/uv run --locked ruff check packages/connectors/hammertime/src tests/test_hammertime_adapter.py tests/support/hammertime_fixture.py: All checks passed.
- .tools/bin/uv run --locked ruff format --check packages/connectors/hammertime/src tests/test_hammertime_adapter.py tests/support/hammertime_fixture.py: 7 files already formatted.
- .tools/bin/uv run --locked mypy packages/domain/src packages/connectors/hammertime/src: Success, no issues found in 11 source files.
- .tools/bin/uv lock --check: Resolved 106 packages.
- .tools/bin/uv run --locked python scripts/check_fixture_safety.py: fixture safety valid, 4 files.
- .tools/bin/uv run --locked python scripts/check_secrets.py: secret scan valid, no findings outside reviewed baseline.
- git diff --check: PASS.
- ASCII dash scan over the five correction files: no prohibited Unicode dash findings.

### Acceptance criteria evidence
- All returned source data is pinned. Tests cover release manifests, alias snapshots, resolved releases, decomposition state and records, general artifacts, hash verification, typed legacy path resolution, registry provenance, legacy matter records, validation reports, packet facts, packet review artifacts, and owner directions.
- Authorization-first tests prove denied callers receive MatterAccessDenied for both existing and missing legacy identifiers, and still receive denial when the registry is absent. No registry or path existence is disclosed before authorization.
- Symlink tests prove fixed internal files and directories cannot escape the configured root or enter synthetic Inbox. Descriptor-level checks enforce exact rooted targets.
- Read-only enforcement tests run the full public surface on a read-only fixture and scan the package for write calls and write-like APIs.
- Static scans confirm frontend and domain code do not construct HammerTime storage paths directly.
- The discovery gate now automatically includes this test module.

### Known limitations
- Secure descriptor verification requires Linux-style /proc/self/fd plus O_NOFOLLOW and O_DIRECTORY. Construction fails closed with AdapterUnavailableError when the required open flags are absent, and reads fail closed if descriptor path verification is unavailable.
- Decomposition citation and relationship entries remain lossless raw mappings because their upstream schema is outside this card.
- Registry resolution intentionally has no full-tree fallback.
- Qdrant and FalkorDB retrieval remain SKL-S2-04 scope.
- No HammerTime Inbox or real protected corpus was inspected during correction or verification.

### Migration and rollback
No data migration or external mutation occurred. Rollback is to revert the five correction files listed above. The package registration and lockfile from the original implementation remain unchanged. No commit or push was made.

Scope finding: the brokered host-execution boundary already exists in scripts/clean_room_check.py (ExternalBrokerSet parent-owned Docker/GPG adapters, loopback-only _LoopbackBroker with token authentication via hmac.compare_digest, _BrokerLimits/_BrokerBudget request/worker/process budgets, _capture_external bounded streaming output with per-command and cumulative limits, two-phase signal-masked atomic start and idempotent close, Landlock sandbox excluding docker/gpg/systemd executables and mediating MAKE_SOCK, git hook and fsmonitor neutralization, descriptor-stable symlink/hardlink/path-swap denial, scratch-root anchor validation, and a terminal machine-readable receipt emitted on every success/failure/timeout/cancellation path in run()). Existing suite tests/test_clean_room_check.py covers these (50 tests). The residual qualification gap was unproven token/socket/atomic-start boundary properties; this card adds exactly that proof and nothing else.

Files changed:
- tests/test_clean_room_broker_boundary.py (new, auto-discovered; 4 hermetic tests: wrong/missing/extra-key/cross-tool token requests are denied with exit 126 and never leak the token; broker endpoints are loopback-only and distinct with a 32-plus-character token; failed start is atomic, never resumes, and closes cleanly; .clean-bin shims are the only docker/gpg entry points, mode 0700, non-symlink, byte-identical to the pinned shim, and lead child PATH).

Individual stages from this tree: type-check exit 0 (mypy: Success, no issues found in 56 source files); unit-test exit 0 (all discovered modules green, including this new module at count=4); integration-test 34 passed, 69 subtests passed in 88.36s (stage exit 2 was a concurrent mid-run edit of scripts/run_checks.sh by the vendoring card, not a test failure); migration-check exit 0; fixture-check exit 0; sbom exit 0; design-hashes, compose-check, lock-check, license-audit passed inside gate runs 1 and 2.

Parent-owned broker with bounded streaming output and request/worker/process budgets, atomic startup/cleanup: ExternalBrokerSet is created and started by the parent controller before containment starts (scripts/clean_room_check.py run() brokers-started phase); _capture_external enforces per-command max_output_bytes and a cumulative max_external_output_bytes budget and kills the process group on breach; _BrokerBudget bounds requests, request/response bytes, workers, and external processes; start is two-phase and signal-masked with full rollback, close is idempotent; proven by test_broker_start_is_atomic_and_never_resumes_after_failure plus existing tests test_loopback_broker_start_is_two_phase_and_partial_threads_join, test_run_registers_two_phase_broker_before_start_failure, test_external_output_is_streamed_bounded_and_processes_are_killed, test_external_output_cumulative_budget_and_input_are_bounded, test_broker_budgets_requests_files_outputs_workers_and_one_keyring, test_wire_budget_counts_every_byte_and_uses_a_fixed_worker_pool.

done.title: [SKL-S2-07][M] Reconcile policy revisions across caches and derived stores
done.description:
## Completion evidence (kimi-skl-s2-07, 2026-08-21)

Implemented policy-revision propagation and reconciliation across request caches and derived stores in the audit package, built against the SKL-S1-05 outbox and SKL-S1-04 policy interfaces. Per AMENDMENT-SKL-S2-10 the work targets PostgreSQL-derived state only; Qdrant and FalkorDB appear nowhere in the implementation. No dependency on the open retrieval cards c4ef2a90 or f5ed9d24.

### Files changed

- packages/audit/src/sklegal_audit/reconciliation.py (new): DerivedRecordPin (source material ID/version/SHA256, policy revision, optional rights revision, retrieval projection set/generation pins required for retrieval store kinds and forbidden otherwise, exact core watermark sequence and hash), DerivedStore and PolicyRevisionOutbox ports, InMemoryDerivedStore (deny-before-purge, idempotent deny/purge, synchronous require_current read gate), PolicyRevisionReconciler (outbox polling with idempotent delivery receipts, per tenant+matter PolicyRevisionView committed before denial so partial failure fails closed at the gate, compare-and-set projection watermark via advance_watermark, separate asynchronous purge, content-free ReconciliationReport with complete per-store counts).
- packages/audit/src/sklegal_audit/ledger.py: added InMemoryAuditLedger.event(tenant_id, event_id) read accessor that verifies the tenant chain before returning one exact event (additive, no behavior change to existing methods).
- packages/audit/src/sklegal_audit/__init__.py: exports for the new reconciliation symbols.
- tests/test_audit_reconciliation.py (new): 29 tests, auto-discovered by the gate runner.
- docs/development/AUDIT.md: new "Policy-revision reconciliation (SKL-S2-07)" section.

### Tests and exact results

- .tools/bin/uv run --locked pytest tests/test_audit_reconciliation.py -q: 29 passed.
- Gate runner ./scripts/run_checks.sh unit-test: tests/test_audit_reconciliation.py 29 passed under the per-module runner; all unit modules pass except the concurrently edited foreign tests/test_policy_governance.py (see known limitations). Modules not reached by the runner after that failure were run separately: 127 passed, 88 subtests passed.
- ./scripts/run_checks.sh integration-test: exit 0.
- Aggregate verification: unit 552 passed + 409 subtests; integration 44 passed, 15 skipped, 120 subtests.
- .tools/bin/uv run --locked ruff check scripts tests services packages: All checks passed. ruff format --check passes on every file except three foreign in-progress governance files.
- .tools/bin/uv run --locked mypy services packages: 5 errors, all in the foreign in-progress packages/policies/src/sklegal_policies/governance.py (GovernanceCommand attr-defined); zero errors in my files.
- migration-check: 12 migrations valid. fixture-check: valid. secret-scan: no findings outside reviewed baseline. sbom: exit 0. vulnerability-scan: exit 0 (pip-audit clean, npm audit 0). npm format:check, lint, typecheck, build, test (85 passed): all pass.
- ./scripts/run_checks.sh all: gate-exit=1 at run_format_check, solely because of three concurrently edited foreign files (packages/policies/src/sklegal_policies/governance.py, services/api/src/sklegal_api/governance.py, tests/test_policy_governance.py) that fail ruff format --check. All other gate steps verified individually green as listed above. No file I touched fails any gate step.

### Acceptance-criteria evidence

- Every derived record carries source, policy, rights, projection, and watermark pins: DerivedRecordPin validation tests (retrieval pins required, cache pins reject projection fields, nil IDs rejected).
- Authorization rechecked before use: require_current gate tests (happy path, wrong revision, unknown, superseded, cross-tenant, cross-matter, rollback evidence, entry ahead of view).
- Stale denied before asynchronous purge: deny_is_idempotent_and_purge_requires_denial; reconciler purge only removes DENIED_STALE (test_purge_removes_only_denied_records, early purge purges 0).
- Invalidation idempotent and observable: test_reconcile_is_idempotent (second run zero new denials, same watermark), deny/purge repeat counts zero, per-store ReconciliationReport counts.
- Outage, lag, rollback, partial failure, revocation races fail closed: test_outbox_outage_fails_closed, test_store_outage_fails_closed_without_watermark_advance (view committed before denial; durable watermark proven unadvanced by external CAS), test_watermark_conflict_fails_closed (denials stand, gate denies with committed view), test_stale_writer_after_reconcile_is_denied, raced reader holding a superseded view still denied by the state marker.
- Reconciler reports complete counts without exposing denied detail: test_report_contains_no_denied_detail (serialized report contains no partition keys, material IDs, matter IDs, or superseded revisions).
- No raw protected content in audit or telemetry: all models reuse the strict AuditValue base; pins and reports carry only UUIDs, safe codes, digests, and counts.
- Outbox integration: test_sink_recorded_decisions_flow_through_outbox drives reconciliation from real DurableAuditSink-recorded PolicyDecision events.

### Known limitations

- Full gate ./scripts/run_checks.sh all currently exits 1 at format-check and would also fail type-check and one unit module due to a concurrent in-progress governance card (files: packages/policies/src/sklegal_policies/governance.py, services/api/src/sklegal_api/governance.py, tests/test_policy_governance.py; failing test GovernanceRaceTests.test_concurrent_supersede_exactly_one_wins, 1 != 0). All unrelated to this card; not touched per swarm rules.
- In-memory adapters are isolated-development only; the durable PostgreSQL outbox consumer must apply effect and receipt in one transaction (documented in docs/development/AUDIT.md).
- Rights revision is carried as an optional pin; active rights-revision propagation awaits the rights model from a later card.
- Reconciler instance keeps its watermark expectation in process; a restart against an existing durable watermark fails closed on WatermarkConflict and requires operator recovery.

done.title: CMDB discovery: derive connects_to edges (service->port, container networks)
done.description:
## Completion evidence (kimi-skcoord-connects-to, 2026-08-22)

Merged to skcoord main as d3f9d2a (implementation 0a38208); pushed. Branch deleted.

## What shipped

- src/skcoord/discovery_connects.py (new, 328 lines; discovery.py only gained 13 wiring lines so the 500-line debt card 74ea00dd stays unblocked): collect_port_service_links attributes each listener to its systemd unit or runtime container via read-only /proc/<pid>/cgroup parsing (deepest *.service wins, user@uid.service excluded, docker-/containerd-/libpod- scopes prefix-matched to container names); edges only to units present in the loaded-units list, no edge when attribution is uncertain; collect_container_networks emits host-qualified NETWORK CIs (<host>:<network>) plus membership edges from read-only docker/podman network ls/inspect, default bridge edged deliberately
- Edge direction: relationship rides on the owning SERVICE CI pointing at the PORT or NETWORK CI, matching the existing subject-carries-relationship convention; connects_to permits every CI type target per ALLOWED_RELATIONSHIPS
- No cross-node edges and deliberately no hook for them; no secret-looking attribute keys (asserted against the PR#25 sanitizer)

## Verification

- 14 new tests (FakeRunner: attribution happy paths, user-slice unwrap, short-id prefix match, unattributable -> no edge, unloaded unit -> no edge, ss -p denied -> partial coverage, ephemeral skip, network membership incl podman lowercase shape, malformed JSON skipped, secret-key hygiene, 2 scan-level pipeline tests)
- Adjacent discovery/cmdb suites 109 passed; full suite 316 passed, 0 failed; ruff clean; fixture shapes validated against this host's real ss output

## Known limitations

- Port attribution re-executes ss/systemctl rather than sharing base collector results (pipeline independence); scan merge folds duplicates
- First pid wins on multi-process (SO_REUSEPORT) listeners
- Unreadable runtime socket during attribution yields partial coverage, logged

done.title: [SKMemory] Fail closed when pgvector reconcile transport is unavailable
done.description:
## Completion evidence (kimi-skmemory-pgvector-failclosed, 2026-08-22)

Merged to skmemory main as 6b6fc14 (implementation 5708f48); pushed. Release tag cut by publish workflow. Branch deleted; clone retained at /tmp/skmemory-dev.

## Root-cause refinement

The vendored reconcile.py already checked returncodes; the incident's residual defects were (1) no transport validation before the first counting query, so a dead transport was indistinguishable from an empty store downstream, and (2) cli sync_cmd phase 3 caught every reconcile exception and exited 0, so the timer run looked clean with a dead transport. Both fixed.

## What shipped

- reconcile.py: ReconcileTransportError; probe_transport() (select 1) before any counting query or mutation; transport labeling without secrets; stderr scrubbing (password= and ://user:pass@ forms); stderr-marker classification (permission denied, daemon connect, no such container, refused/failed) so transport failures never read as SQL errors; OSError missing-binary wrapped as transport error; prune guard and DSN-first choice untouched
- cli.py: phase-3 reconcile failure now warns and exits 1 (one intentional behavior-contract change; the old test pinning exit-0 was rewritten to pin exit 1)
- dsn_psql.py: DSN password redaction in error output
- pg_migrate.py audited and left untouched (already checks every returncode and redacts)

## Verification

- 10 new regression tests (permission-denied fake transport: raises before mutation, only the probe reaches the transport, zero mutating SQL, no pg=0 stats; mid-run counting failure aborts; happy path intact; CLI exit 1 hermetic via SKMEMORY_HOME)
- 60 new+adjacent tests passed; broader pg/CLI 82 passed; full suite 1270 passed, 206 skipped (live-service), 0 failed; ruff check + format clean

## Known limitations / follow-ups

- Transport classification is stderr-marker based; an exotic failure classifies as query error but still raises before mutation (fail closed holds)
- Probe validates at run start; a mid-run transport death aborts at that call, mutations already applied stay applied (reconcile never claimed atomicity)
- Phase 4 (--graph AGE) keeps warn-and-continue behavior; out of scope here, candidate for a sibling card (c25e2513 territory)
acceptance_criteria: Permission-denied and missing-container tests fail closed before any backfill/prune.
Reconcile reports the actual governed node-local database and never treats query failure as an empty set.
CLI returns nonzero on vector reconciliation failure and preserves actionable redacted diagnostics.

- skmemory/graph_reconcile.py: graph_parity() dry-run report (flat/graph/matched/stale/missing with explicit id lists, GraphTransportError on dead graph instead of phantom zeros); reconcile_graph() with dry-run default, the LITERAL shared pgvector prune_guard imported from skmemory.reconcile (floor SKMEMORY_GRAPH_PRUNE_FLOOR=1, fraction 0.20, min-sample 20, force SKMEMORY_GRAPH_RECONCILE_FORCE), timestamped JSON backup (nodes plus incident edge inventory) before any delete, per-id remove_memory DETACH DELETE with abort-on-failure, zero-incident-edge aux cleanup with per-label counts; tombstoned ids prune from the graph, tier-race-vanished files stay authoritative (fail closed), invalid-id files excluded without quarantining (report path never mutates the flat store)

done.title: [SKL-S4-07][S] Specify the outbox vs Temporal connector-dispatch ownership boundary
done.description:
## Outcome

AGENTS.md and AUDIT.md place connector dispatch on the polled PG outbox; Sprint 3/4 cards place connector workflows in Temporal. No document assigns ownership, and S4-06 (XL) will hit this first. One paragraph now prevents double-dispatch drift later.

## Scope

- Decide which mechanism owns connector dispatch and which owns derived projections; document the handoff and idempotency interaction.
- Amend TDD section 14 or AUDIT.md through the approval trail.
- Reference the decision from every S4-06 child card.

## Completion evidence (kimi-skl-s4-07, 2026-08-21)

Decision: Temporal owns connector dispatch orchestration (validation, exact-version Approval binding, destination and capability verification, provider call, receipt capture, reconciliation, retries, human waits); only a Temporal activity may invoke a provider adapter, simulation mode by default. The polled PostgreSQL outbox (migration 0007) owns the content-free evidence handoff and derived projections only; it never initiates a provider call. Double dispatch is prevented by one owner plus one dedup record: the dispatch activity reuses the record_outbox_delivery idempotency pattern (deterministic SHA-256 over tenant, action identity, destination, approved artifact hash), claims the key before the provider call, returns the recorded receipt on retry, and fails closed when approval, capability, destination verification, or the audit append is unavailable.

Files changed:
- docs/development/AUDIT.md: new section "Connector dispatch ownership (SKL-S4-07)" after "Transactional outbox and projections". AUDIT.md chosen over TDD section 14 because the TDD is hash-pinned in docs/approval/DESIGN-HASHES.sha256; the amendment explicitly states it supplements TDD section 14 without altering approved documents and takes effect through the card review and approval trail.

Acceptance criteria evidence:
- "Approved ownership paragraph merged into the design docs": ownership section merged into docs/development/AUDIT.md; approval step is this card's human review.
- "All S4-06 child cards reference the decision": doc link docs/development/AUDIT.md#connector-dispatch-ownership-skl-s4-07 attached via skcapstone coord link to 38798f6c (S4-06A), f3c55ccd (S4-06B), 5b3ab1fe (S4-06C), 1331e2fb (S4-06D), 6de72db6 (S4-06E), e180fe3d (S4-06F).

Tests run:
- .venv/bin/python -m unittest tests.test_audit: Ran 11 tests, OK.
- sha256sum --check docs/approval/DESIGN-HASHES.sha256: all 5 pinned documents OK (proves no approved document was altered).
- ./scripts/run_checks.sh secret-scan: "secret scan valid: no findings outside reviewed baseline".
- grep -nP '[\x{2013}\x{2014}]' docs/development/AUDIT.md: no em or en dashes.

Known limitations:
- Docs and contract card: no runtime code changed, so no new unit tests apply; the audit contract suite was rerun to confirm the spec still matches implemented behavior.
- The outbox delivery idempotency key is keyed by audit event hash today; S4-06A must implement the analogous action-level key (tenant, action identity, destination, approved artifact hash) for the dispatch path as specified.

done.title: [SKL-S3-09][S] Measure per-tenant audit chain-head write serialization
done.description:
## Outcome

The append-only audit design serializes all appends for a tenant through one locked chain-head row. Quantify the throughput ceiling before multi-tenant claims are made.

## Scope

- Microbenchmark concurrent appends for a single tenant at realistic event rates.
- Publish ops/sec ceiling and lock-wait profile.
- If the ceiling is low, propose mitigation (per-matter chains, batching) as a follow-up card.

## Completion evidence (kimi-skl-s3-09, 2026-08-21)

### Outcome
Measured the per-tenant audit chain-head serialization ceiling of migration
0007's append_event (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE on the single chain_heads row per
tenant). Published ceiling: roughly 80 to 96 appends/sec per tenant on the
benchmark host; throughput peaks at 2 concurrent writers (96.25 ops/sec) and
degrades to 80.07 ops/sec at 32 writers; p99 append latency grows from 26 ms
(1 writer) to 655 ms (32 writers); lock waiters present in ~100% of monitor
samples at 4+ writers; two-tenant control (8 workers per tenant) delivered
170.59 ops/sec aggregate, a 1.983x speedup over the single-tenant 8-worker
level, confirming the serialization boundary is per tenant. Both tenant hash
chains verified after 15,800 total appends; deadlock delta 0.

### Files changed
- scripts/benchmark_audit_chain_head.py (new): self-contained benchmark driver
  (disposable pinned Postgres 17.7 container, full migration chain, provisioned
  RLS-bound runtime roles, persistent psql worker sessions, server-side
  clock_timestamp latency bracketing, 10 ms pg_stat_activity lock-wait monitor,
  two-tenant control, chain verification).
- tests/test_audit_chain_head_benchmark.py (new): 10 unit tests for stats and
  payload helpers plus 1 docker smoke test running the real benchmark at tiny
  scale.
- docs/evidence/audit/SKL-S3-09-CHAIN-HEAD-SERIALIZATION-2026-08-21.md (new):
  method, environment, full results table, interpretation, limitations.
- build/audit/chain-head-benchmark.json (generated artifact, not committed);
  sha256 2b4d5301bb29fd1a419248345bd9ff4fedba8c374f40283cf716e18d5cf98911.
- No shared package code, migrations, or run_checks.sh modified.

### Tests run (exact commands and results)
- .tools/bin/uv run --locked python -m unittest tests.test_audit_chain_head_benchmark -v
  -> Ran 11 tests in 21.880s, OK (incl. containerized smoke test: chain
  verified, 30/30 events, 0 deadlocks, two-tenant control 20 events).
- .tools/bin/uv run --locked ruff check scripts/benchmark_audit_chain_head.py tests/test_audit_chain_head_benchmark.py -> All checks passed.
- .tools/bin/uv run --locked ruff format --check (same files) -> 2 files already formatted.
- .tools/bin/uv run --locked python -m unittest tests.test_audit -> Ran 11 tests, OK (regression check of the untouched audit package).
- Full benchmark: .tools/bin/uv run --locked python scripts/benchmark_audit_chain_head.py --label chiap01-workstation-2026-08-21-r2 --output build/audit/chain-head-benchmark.json -> exit 0, chain verified: True.

### Acceptance criteria evidence
1. "Published single-tenant append throughput ceiling with method": ceiling
   80-96 ops/sec per tenant with full method in
   docs/evidence/audit/SKL-S3-09-CHAIN-HEAD-SERIALIZATION-2026-08-21.md and raw
   data in build/audit/chain-head-benchmark.json.
2. "Mitigation follow-up card created if the ceiling threatens Sprint 5 load
   targets": ceiling is low in absolute terms (per-tenant cap under ~100
   ops/sec, contention from 2 writers, p99 over 600 ms at 32 writers).
   Follow-up card 2a41d17d created proposing per-matter chains and/or batch
   append. Sprint 5 pilot steady-state load is far below the ceiling, so the
   pilot is not blocked; the follow-up gates multi-tenant load claims.

### Known limitations
- Numbers are host-specific (24 logical CPUs, tmpfs, pinned postgres:17.7-alpine
  image); the serialization shape is a property of the design.

  shared file is being edited by other agents in flight; run it explicitly.

### Migration/rollback notes
No data or schema changes; the benchmark uses a disposable --rm container with
tmpfs storage and removes it on exit. Nothing to roll back.

done.title: [SKL-S3-09-FU] Mitigate audit chain-head serialization ceiling (per-matter chains or batch append)
done.description:
## Outcome

SKL-S3-09 (card 1b0a7b29) measured the append-only audit chain-head
serialization design. The single-tenant append ceiling is roughly 80 to 96
ops/sec on the benchmark host, contention starts at 2 concurrent writers, and
p99 append latency exceeds 600 ms at 32 writers. Throughput cannot scale per
tenant because every append locks the single sklegal_audit.chain_heads row
for the tenant. Evidence: docs/evidence/audit/SKL-S3-09-CHAIN-HEAD-SERIALIZATION-2026-08-21.md.

## Scope

- Evaluate per-matter (or per-partition) chain heads so independent matters
  of one tenant append concurrently while preserving per-chain integrity and
  tenant-wide verification.
- Evaluate batch append (one chain-head lock acquisition per N events) as an
  alternative or complement.
- Decide and record whether the mitigation is needed before multi-tenant load
  claims in Sprint 5 and later.

## Constraints

- Any design change must preserve the append-only, hash-chained,
  controlled-writer, FORCE RLS guarantees of migration 0007.
- Verification and rollback detection must still detect evidence-bearing
  rollback per tenant.

## Completion evidence (kimi, 2026-08-21)

Decision recorded and proposed through the approval trail.

### Files changed

- docs/architecture/AUDIT-CHAIN-SCALING.md (new): the governing chain-scaling
  decision. Evaluates per-Matter chain heads (concurrency win, but
  chain-scoped sequences, vector projection watermarks, and loss of the
  Tenant-wide cryptographic total order) and batch append (rejected as the
  primary mitigation: cross-transaction batching breaks the atomic
  mutation-plus-audit-plus-outbox guarantee; in-transaction batching stays
  permitted as a local optimization).
- docs/approval/AMENDMENT-SKL-S3-09-FU.md (new): amendment record, status
  proposed, pending human approval. No hash-pinned document modified; no
  migration, code, or deployment authorized.
- tests/test_audit_chain_scaling_decision.py (new): 5 contract tests pinning
  the measurement basis, the decision, the trigger gate, the amendment
  status, and a fail-closed guard that no migration other than 0007 touches
  chain_heads while the schema change is deferred.

### Decision

1. No schema change before or during the Sprint 5 pilot; the single-chain
   design stands (pilot load is far below the measured ceiling and no
   numeric Sprint 5 audit-rate target exists yet; S5-04B owns the load
   envelope).
2. Per-Matter chain heads are the design direction if a mitigation is
   required, with genesis anchoring to the Tenant tip, per-chain plus
   Tenant-wide aggregate verification, and vector projection watermarks as
   documented preconditions.
3. Numeric trigger gate: sustained over 50 appends/sec per Tenant, p99
   append latency over 100 ms at pilot concurrency, or any multi-tenant
   load claim beyond the pilot.

### Tests and exact results

- .tools/bin/uv run --locked python -m unittest tests.test_audit_chain_scaling_decision: Ran 5 tests, OK.
- .tools/bin/uv run --locked ruff check tests/test_audit_chain_scaling_decision.py: All checks passed.
- .tools/bin/uv run --locked ruff format --check tests/test_audit_chain_scaling_decision.py: already formatted.

### Known limitations

- The evaluation is analytical, grounded in the S3-09 measurement and the
  migration 0007 source; no per-Matter prototype was benchmarked. When the
  trigger gate fires, the first implementation card must re-run
  scripts/benchmark_audit_chain_head.py for before and after numbers.
- The amendment is proposed and pending human approval; until approved, the
  document is proposed architecture guidance and the single-chain design
  remains authoritative.

### Migration and rollback

No data, schema, or shared code changed. Rollback is removal of the three
new files.

done.title: [SKL-S1-13][S] Vendor or mirror the capauth upstream dependency
done.description:
## Outcome

The authorization core no longer depends on a single personal GitHub repository pinned to one commit.

## Scope

- Mirror github.com/smilinTux/capauth under organizational control or vendor it into the repo with hash verification.
- Update the pin, SBOM, and pip-audit surrogate handling accordingly.
- Document the update path for future upstream revisions.

## Completion evidence (kimi-skl-s1-13, 2026-08-21)

Chosen approach: vendor the upstream tree into `vendor/capauth` at the exact pinned commit `183c04a7c623e8abcf37bd705bf8bca1deb4a364` with per-file SHA256 enforcement, wired as a uv path source so installs and exports never fetch the personal remote. An organizational git mirror was the alternative; creating an external mirror repository or account is outside this agent's authority, so the external remainder is: optionally mirror upstream under organizational control later and switch `tool.uv.sources` to that remote; the vendored copy satisfies both acceptance criteria on its own.

### Files changed

- `vendor/capauth/**` (new): vendored CapAuth 0.3.1 source (LICENSE, MANIFEST.in, README.md, pyproject.toml, src/) byte-identical to upstream commit 183c04a7c623e8abcf37bd705bf8bca1deb4a364 except the documented build patch (static version replaces setuptools_scm dynamic versioning; recorded under `local_modifications`).
- `vendor/capauth/VENDOR-MANIFEST.json` (new): provenance manifest with upstream URL, pinned commit, version, include/exclude lists, and SHA256 for all 136 vendored files.
- `vendor/README.md` (new): vendoring policy summary.
- `scripts/check_vendor_capauth.py` (new): verifier; fails closed on hash mismatch, missing or unrecorded files, symlinks, wrong pinned commit/version, or any residual personal-remote reference in `pyproject.toml`, `packages/capauth/pyproject.toml`, or `uv.lock`. `--write-manifest` regenerates the manifest for future updates.
- `tests/test_vendor_capauth.py` (new): 9 contract tests (manifest match, wiring, pin constants, installed package resolves inside vendor/capauth, tamper/missing/unrecorded/wrong-commit detection).
- `packages/capauth/pyproject.toml`: dependency changed from the git-plus-commit pin to `capauth==0.3.1`.
- `pyproject.toml`: `tool.uv.sources` gains `capauth = { path = "vendor/capauth", editable = true }`.
- `uv.lock`: capauth source is now `editable = "vendor/capauth"`; no smilinTux remote remains.
- `scripts/run_checks.sh`: vulnerability scan runs the vendor verifier, requires exactly one `-e ./vendor/capauth` exported requirement, rejects any personal-remote reference, keeps the `capauth==0.3.1` pip-audit surrogate (preserving the d5457c69 surrogate path), and keeps `--require-hashes` pip-audit for registry packages; mypy list gains `scripts/check_vendor_capauth.py`.
- `scripts/check_secrets.py`: detect-secrets excludes `vendor/` (hash-pinned verbatim third-party tree, same treatment as node_modules/uv.lock).
- `docs/development/CAPAUTH.md`: provenance section now describes the vendored copy and documents the update path for future upstream revisions.
- `README.md`: CapAuth bullet notes the vendored location.

### Tests and exact results

- `.tools/bin/uv run --locked pytest -v tests/test_vendor_capauth.py`: 9 passed, 0 failed.
- `./scripts/run_checks.sh vulnerability-scan`: exit 0 ("vendored capauth verified: 136 files, version 0.3.1, upstream commit 183c04a7..."; pip-audit "No known vulnerabilities found" for registry requirements and the capauth==0.3.1 surrogate; npm audit 0 vulnerabilities).
- `./scripts/run_checks.sh sbom`: exit 0 (build/sbom/python.cdx.json carries capauth 0.3.1).
- `./scripts/run_checks.sh secret-scan`: exit 0 ("no findings outside reviewed baseline").
- `./scripts/run_checks.sh unit-test`: exit 0 (31 modules discovered, all passed; includes test_vendor_capauth.py, 552 PASSED lines).
- `./scripts/run_checks.sh integration-test`: exit 0 (includes the real-OpenPGP capauth contract test, passed).
- `./scripts/run_checks.sh migration-check`, `fixture-check`, `lint`: exit 0.
- `./scripts/run_checks.sh all`: exit 1 at format-check, blocked by concurrent in-flight work from another card, not by this change: `packages/policies/src/sklegal_policies/governance.py` and `services/api/src/sklegal_api/governance.py` are unformatted (ruff), and the same `sklegal_policies/governance.py` has 5 mypy attr-defined errors (`GovernanceCommand` has no attribute `action`). None of the failing files are touched by this card; every gate stage passes when run individually against this card's files. The full run passed design hashes, compose check, lock check, and license audit before stopping at format-check.

### Acceptance criteria evidence

1. "Build no longer fetches capauth from the personal remote at install time": `uv sync --locked --all-packages` installs `capauth==0.3.1 (from file:///.../vendor/capauth)`; `uv.lock` and both pyproject manifests contain no `smilinTux/capauth` reference (enforced by `scripts/check_vendor_capauth.py` and by the vulnerability-scan grep that fails the gate if the personal remote appears in exported requirements).
2. "SBOM and vuln-scan scripts pass against the vendored or mirrored source": both stages exit 0 as shown above; the exact pinned commit and per-file hashes remain enforced through VENDOR-MANIFEST.json.

### Known limitations

- The vendored pyproject carries one documented local patch: static `version = "0.3.1"` replaces setuptools_scm (no git metadata in the vendored tree).
- Upstream optional extras (service, dev, gnupg, skcapstone, all) remain declared but are not locked or installed; only base dependencies are resolved, matching the prior behavior.
- Vendored content is verbatim upstream and keeps upstream editorial style; it is excluded from SKLegal lint, format, type-check, and secret-scan targets, with integrity enforced by the hash manifest instead.
- `./scripts/run_checks.sh all` cannot be green until the concurrent policy-governance card's files are formatted and type-clean; this is documented above, not patched around.
- No organizational external mirror was created (requires an external account/repo creation outside this agent's authority); vendoring fully satisfies the card locally, and the mirror remains an optional future hardening step.

### Rollback

Remove the `capauth` path source from `pyproject.toml`, restore the git-plus-commit pin in `packages/capauth/pyproject.toml`, run `uv lock`, delete `vendor/`, `scripts/check_vendor_capauth.py`, and `tests/test_vendor_capauth.py`, and restore the prior `run_vulnerability_scan` git-pin check in `scripts/run_checks.sh`. No database or data migration is involved.
acceptance_criteria: Build no longer fetches capauth from the personal remote at install time
SBOM and vuln-scan scripts pass against the vendored or mirrored source

## Outcome

Small correctness and drift-risk fixes in the CapAuth package and deploy config.

## Scope

- packages/capauth/src/sklegal_capauth/authorization.py: expose child issuance as a public CapabilityIssuer API instead of the _issue_child private reach-through.
- Deduplicate the attenuation logic into one function with the principal-type allowance table defined once.
- Deploy: add postgres.env.example, add a *.env gitignore rule, document local setup, and drop the redundant function-local import json in packages/capauth/src/sklegal_capauth/postgres.py.

## Completion evidence 2026-08-21

- Public CapabilityIssuer.issue_child added. All 8 production and test reach-throughs migrated. Static scan found zero ._issue_child calls.
- One _is_attenuated implementation and one principal allowance table now govern both preflight and signed-chain validation. Depth, max-depth, time, use-limit, tenant, principal-type, exact scalar, and optional narrowing rules remain fail closed.
- deploy/chiap01/postgres.env.example provides POSTGRES_DB, POSTGRES_USER, and placeholder POSTGRES_PASSWORD. deploy/chiap01/README.md documents copy, edit, config validation, start, and stop. *.env is ignored and *.env.example is committable.
- Focused CapAuth suite: 32 tests passed. Deploy hygiene: 1 test passed. Docker Compose example config: exit 0. Independent acceptance review: PASS.
- Full ./scripts/run_checks.sh all before and after: exit 0. Post-change run passed formatting, lint, type checks, web build and 85 web tests, unit suites, real PostgreSQL 34-test contract with 69 subtests, secret scan, vendor integrity, and vulnerability audits. The 15 host-only clean-room containment tests remained skipped by their explicit opt-in gate.
- Files changed: .gitignore; deploy/chiap01/README.md; deploy/chiap01/postgres.env.example; packages/capauth/src/sklegal_capauth/authorization.py; packages/capauth/src/sklegal_capauth/postgres.py; packages/capauth/src/sklegal_capauth/tokens.py; tests/test_capauth_authorization.py; tests/test_capauth_boundaries.py; tests/test_capauth_delegation.py; tests/test_deploy_env_hygiene.py.
- No production service started, no data changed, no migration applies, and no commit or push was made. Source-only rollback is review of the workspace diff or a reviewed revert after commit.

## Release evidence 2026-08-21

- Committed as d14ca7e8f39e2c05f02ab00746683b16c7487d9b.
- Included in annotated tag v0.4.0 at 9a82f100d8cdda4ffdb2c3daaf0f04abae441cd7.
- Pushed to origin/main and the remote v0.4.0 tag after a clean-HEAD ./scripts/run_checks.sh all exit 0.
- The earlier no-commit statement records the implementation handoff state and is superseded by this release evidence.

Attenuation rules exist in exactly one shared implementation

done.title: [SKSync] Enforce private-material policy at every Syncthing folder root
done.description:
## Completion evidence (kimi-sksync-private-policy, 2026-08-22)

Merged to skcapstone main as 8f07f9b (implementation 41ddd53); pushed. Release tag is cut by the publish workflow on main push. Feature branch deleted; clone retained at /tmp/skcapstone-dev.

## What shipped

- src/skcapstone/sync_policy/ package: fail-closed .stignore evaluator (documented subset: comments, (?d)/(?i), negation -> UNCERTAIN, anchoring, ** components, directory rules, ancestor implication; unsupported anywhere makes every evaluation UNCERTAIN, and UNCERTAIN never counts as covered); pydantic report models; Syncthing config.xml discovery from both standard locations plus --config, tilde expansion, symlink resolution, dedupe; per-folder audit with could-land probes and a pruning walk (200k cap with warn); legacy ~/.capauth detection; duplicate private-fingerprint detection via lazy PGPy; additive idempotent apply_remediation with backup
- skcapstone sync audit CLI: --config/--home/--agent-home/--capauth-home/--json/--apply; dry-run by default; exit 1 on any error-grade finding (fail closed, including missing or malformed config)
- defaults/.stignore and the inline fallback gained the missing private-material rules (*.rev, **/revocation*, **/passphrase*, *.pass, .gnupg/secring.gpg, .gnupg/private-keys-v1.d, **/*.kbx, security/tokens) with load-bearing comments

## Verification

- 58 new tests (synthetic fixtures only, PGPy throwaway keys); adjacent stignore/syncthing suites 108 passed; full suite 6343 passed, 38 skipped, 0 failed (5m43s, isolated venv with editable install)
- black --check and ruff check clean on all changed files (3 pre-existing repo-wide ruff errors untouched)
- Live read-only run against this host's real Syncthing config flagged: ~/.skcapstone missing the new-class rules, the legacy skcapstone-sync folder rooted at ~/.skcapstone/sync has NO .stignore at all, legacy ~/.capauth holds private material, and one real duplicate private fingerprint across locations

## Known limitations

- Negation semantics intentionally fail closed to UNCERTAIN; canonical template has no negations
- security/tokens and capauth/security/tokens asserted non-syncable per the card; a future design that replicates the PDP token store needs a deliberate revert
- Fingerprint parsing requires PGPy; without it the duplicate check degrades to a warn finding
- Follow-up worth scheduling: run skcapstone sync audit on every fleet node and apply remediation (the live findings above are real drift)

done.title: [SKL-S1-14][S] Migration lint: re-created SECURITY DEFINER functions must re-apply privilege hardening
done.description:
## Outcome

Migration lint rule live: re-created SECURITY DEFINER functions must re-apply privilege hardening. Generalizes the 0010 defect (DROP+CREATE lost REVOKE FROM PUBLIC and the sklegal_runtime grant) into a gate.

## Rule as implemented (scripts/check_migrations.py: validate_function_privileges)

Chain-coverage with manifest-order semantics, refined after investigation showed 0001-0005 rely on the 0005 blanket revoke while 0006+ harden in-file:

- A creation is compliant when its own file revokes PUBLIC explicitly, or a blanket REVOKE ALL ON ALL FUNCTIONS IN SCHEMA appears in the same or a strictly later migration. An earlier blanket never covers a later creation (the 0010 defect class).
- DROP plus CREATE loses all privileges: prior grants must be re-applied in the same or a later file. CREATE OR REPLACE preserves privileges and is accepted without re-hardening.
- Regex-based signature normalization (whitespace, case, arg-name stripping), no SQL parser, consistent with the existing checker style.

## Evidence (jarvis, 2026-08-21, after the delegated agent was quota-killed and the spec amendment)

- python scripts/check_migrations.py: 'migration manifest valid: 12 migration(s)' (all real migrations pass)
- python -m unittest tests.test_foundation: 19 tests OK, including 5 new lint tests (blanket coverage accepted, post-blanket creation rejected, DROP+CREATE missing revoke rejected, DROP+CREATE missing grants rejected, CREATE OR REPLACE accepted)
- ruff format/check and mypy clean on touched files
- ./scripts/run_checks.sh all: EXIT=0 (full gate including 34/34 integration tests)
